stops.note: named the reddish seeds of the annatto shrub used as dye and seasoning
stops.meaning: the seed of the annatto shrub

stops.note: the Aztecs used the seeds to colour food and body paint, and Spanish kept the Nahuatl name
stops.meaning: a red seasoning and dye made from annatto seeds

stops.note: the English ex-Dominican friar Thomas Gage described it as early as 1648 in 'The English-American', his account of years spent in New Spain
stops.meaning: a red-orange seasoning and coloring made from annatto seeds

current_meaning: a red-orange seasoning and natural dye made from the seeds of the annatto shrub
